name: Claude Opus 5.5
archDisplay: Proprietary model; architecture and parameter count undisclosed; adaptive thinking with a runtime effort parameter (low to max), 1M-token context
note: Model id claude-opus-5-5, released 2026-09-22 as 'the first model in our new Claude 5.5 family'. Anthropic says it 'performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5'. Priced at $4/$20 per MTok (20% below Opus 5), with cache reads at $0.20 (60% less than Opus 5). It has a 1M context, 128K max output, adaptive thinking that is always on (it can't be disabled), and medium default effort. It ships with Fable-5.1-class cyber/bio safeguards, and flagged cyber tasks fall back to Opus 4.8. Launch scores were run with safeguards on, which Anthropic says likely depresses some rows.

results.notes: Terminal-Bench 4.0 at XHIGH effort (Anthropic: Opus 5.5's highest score; max is lower). SE ±2.6. System Card §8.5 gives 66.36 with safeguards on (fallback on 2.5% of requests). Table: Fable 5.1 55.8, Opus 5 52.3, GPT-6 Astra 57.9 (high, per OpenAI), GPT-5.6 Sol 37.3. Vals AI's independent mini-swe-agent run (65.15, 2026-10-12) is not filed: 22 of 198 attempts were served by Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 provider fallback (58.08 counting those as failures).

FrontierCode v1.1 (Main), best reasoning effort, which is MEDIUM (the default): System Card §8.4 and the announcement chart caption both say 54.6. The announcement table's max-effort cell is 54.4. Note that SC §8.4 lists Opus 5 at 53.4 (best effort) while the max-effort table lists Opus 5 at 48.0.
FrontierCode v1.1 (Extended), System Card §8.4; ahead of Opus 5 63.6, Fable 5 64.9, GPT-6 Astra 64.5, Fable 5.1 63.6.

AutomationBench (Zapier), max effort. Anthropic footnote: 'run and reported by Zapier... without fallback models, so safeguard interventions were considered failures'. Opus 5.5's result comes from Zapier's early-access evaluation. It is behind GPT-6 Astra's 41.4.
